# craftos-mcp

craftos-mcp is a headless CC:Tweaked (ComputerCraft) emulator with an MCP server: the `craftos_*` tools run Lua
programs on emulated computers, read the terminal and every monitor as text, tap buttons, change the world around the
computer and run tests. Run and test every ComputerCraft program in it before saying it works, and before it goes on
a computer in a real game.

## The development loop

The `craftos-mcp` MCP server runs a forked CraftOS-PC engine (no Minecraft, no GUI) with the real CC:Tweaked ROM:
Minecraft **1.21.1** (CC:Tweaked 1.121.0) by default, or 1.20.1 / 1.18.2 per world (`world.version`). Call
`craftos_info` first; it lists anything missing, the versions and the addons that are on. `craftos_help` gives the
full world schema, the ccunit API and the saved worlds on request.

1. `craftos_write_file` the program (workspace-relative; the workspace is copied to the **root** of
   every emulated computer, so `dofile("surface")` and `require("lib.x")` behave like a real deployment).
2. `craftos_run` it. Pass `monitors: [{name:"top", blocksWide:3, blocksHigh:2}]` to attach monitors the
   way a monitor wall is built (1x1 block = 7x5 chars, 2x2 = 18x12, 3x2 = 29x12 at text scale 1).
   `setTextScale` resizes the grid like CC (5x6 blocks at 0.5 = 100x81; monitors are capped at 8x6 blocks);
   `textScale` in the spec sets it up front. Set `screenshots: true` to see PNGs of every screen. Programs that
   never exit end as `timed_out`; their screens are still captured, which is the normal way to check an idle screen.
3. For interaction use `craftos_session_create`, then `craftos_type`, `craftos_key`,
   `craftos_touch_monitor`, `craftos_wait_for_text`, `craftos_screenshot`, finally
   `craftos_session_destroy`. A viewer is served at http://127.0.0.1:7878 (click monitors, type).
   **Prefer data over pictures.** `craftos_ui` returns every screen as rectangles (buttons, cards,
   panels: colour, size, and the 1-based `cx,cy` cell to touch) plus text runs with colours for text-mode
   screens and a change `hash`, and reports what the program is blocked on (`waiting.blocked/filter`).
   `craftos_act` sends one touch, key or text, waits until the program actually consumed it
   (`consumed:false` means it was not listening) and until the screen stops changing, so no sleeps or
   polling. `craftos_settle` waits for quiet without acting. This works for any script, with no changes
   to it. Use `craftos_screenshot` only when you need to see how something looks. Text drawn with a
   pixel font cannot be read as characters: identify such buttons by colour and position.
   **Cheapest loop (fewest tokens), in this order:**
   - `craftos_labels` once per program: read a button's colour from one `craftos_ui` (or one screenshot), name it
     (`{DOUBLE:{color:"#f15c5c"}}`), `save` it, `load` it next time. Names then show inline in `craftos_ui`.
   - `craftos_script` runs a whole scenario in one call (`touch {name}`, `key`, `text`, `expect`, `sim`,
     `advance`, `seed`, `settle`); it stops at the first failure and returns only that step's reason, the
     nearest things that do exist, and `evidence` file paths (PNGs and a JSON dump) to open only if needed.
   - `craftos_expect` is one assertion batch (rect by colour/name, text, what it is `waiting` on, a sim value by
     path, `changed`).
   - `craftos_ui {delta:true}` after an action returns only what changed; `craftos_sim_state {delta:true}`
     likewise.
   - `craftos_trace` says what the program was handed and printed, plus errors, since the last call: use it
     when something is off instead of screenshots.
   - Determinism: `world.seed` (or `craftos_seed`) pins `math.random` and neutralises the program's own
     `math.randomseed`; `craftos_advance {seconds}` jumps the virtual clock and fires due timers, so
     timeouts and countdowns pass instantly. Only timers due inside the jump fire early.
4. Lock behaviour in with tests (next section).
5. A `craftos.json` at the project root (`npx craftos-mcp init` writes one) gives every call its workspace,
   Minecraft version, addons, test globs (`craftos_test` with no `paths` runs those) and base world; `craftos_info`
   names it as `project`. Arguments still win. Outside the agent, `npx craftos-mcp doctor` checks the engine, ROMs,
   cache, craftos.json, world files and a hello-world boot, with a fix for each failure.

## Testing CC programs

Put `*.test.lua` files in the workspace and call `craftos_test` (or run `npx craftos-mcp test` in a terminal; it exits
1 on a failure, and `--watch` reruns the affected files on every save). Each file runs in its own fresh computer.
Inside, use the global `ccunit`:

- `test(name, fn [, {timeout}])`: one test; with a timeout it fails instead of hanging the file.
- `eq` (compares tables deeply), `neq`, `near(a, b [, within])`, `contains(haystack, needle)`, `truthy`, `raises`,
  `skip(name)`.
- `run(program, {seconds | script, args})` runs a program as the shell would and returns `{ok, done, screen}`;
  `screen(monitor?)` reads a monitor's (or the terminal's) lines after it, and `touch(monitor, x, y)` taps a monitor.
  To tap a button, give `run` a `script` function: it runs next to the program, and the run ends when it returns.

```lua
ccunit.test("a tap turns it on", function()
  ccunit.run("button.lua", { script = function()
    sleep(0.5)                  -- let the program draw
    ccunit.touch("top", 3, 2)   -- monitor, column, row
    sleep(0.5)                  -- let it react
  end })
  ccunit.contains(ccunit.screen("top"), "ON")
end)
```

A hanging file keeps its finished tests and names the one it was in. A failed `craftos_run` comes back with
`error {kind, message, file, line}`. For screen layout use `craftos_run` with `snapshot: {name}` (golden files in
`__snapshots__/`; `update:true` to accept). On a big suite give `craftos_test` a `budgetMs`: at the budget it stops and
returns the finished files plus `notRun`. A test's monitors and blocks come from a world file next to it
(`button.world.json` for `button.test.lua`), `world` in craftos.json, or `--world` / `--monitor top:2x1` on the
command line.

## Facts that bite

- Every Advanced Peripherals and inventory method (except getName, getConfiguration, scanCost and the integrator's
  setters) waits a server tick and throws away every event that arrives meanwhile, timers and touches included. A
  loop that re-arms one timer dies the first time it is lost. Make those calls in their own coroutine with parallel.
- The event queue holds 256 events; more are dropped silently.
- A speaker never refuses playSound; playNote is capped at 8 per tick.
- Wireless modems reach 64 blocks low down, up to 384 at the top of the world, and the larger of the two modems'
  ranges counts. Ender modems reach everything in every dimension. Wired names (`computer_N`, `speaker_N`) come from
  a counter, never the computer id.
- rednet numbers messages with `math.random` and drops repeats, so computers on one network need different seeds.
  `createNetwork` refuses a shared one.
- Several computers talking: `craftos_network_create`, one session each, with real rednet.
- The Lua VM follows the CC:Tweaked version the world runs (`world.version`, `--mc`, `CRAFTOS_VERSION`), matched
  against the real Cobalt jars. Minecraft 1.18.2 (CC:Tweaked 1.101.3, Cobalt 0.6): Lua 5.1 semantics,
  no `goto`/`::labels::` (5.1 syntax errors), `_VERSION` is `Lua 5.1`, no 5.2 library extras. Minecraft 1.20.1 and
  1.21.1 (CC:Tweaked 1.121.0, Cobalt 0.9.9, the default): Lua 5.2, with `goto`, `_VERSION` `Lua 5.2`, hex floats,
  `__name`, 5.2 error positions. Pick the version the user's server runs.
- Key codes are GLFW (`keys.enter` = 257), not the old LWJGL values.
- Emulator only, not CC:Tweaked: in the headless runner `os.shutdown(code)` ends the run with that exit status (`0`
  completed, `1` program error, like `shell.run` returning false). Real CC:Tweaked's `os.shutdown()` takes no argument
  and ignores one, so never rely on it in code meant for a server.
- Engine peripherals are vanilla only (monitor, drive, printer). Pass a `world` to `craftos_run` / `craftos_test` /
  `craftos_session_create` for everything else: virtual inventories (chests, barrels) with pushItems/pullItems and
  the blocks of the addons below. During a session `craftos_sim_command` changes the world (players join, chat, items
  appear, the clock jumps) and `craftos_sim_state` reads it, including the computer's own redstone
  (`redstone.outputs.<side>`, inputs, bundled), so check a door opened there, not by printing.
  `craftos_session_create` returns `front: "shell" | "program"`: a startup.lua program that never returns leaves no
  prompt.
- Turtles: give the world a `turtle` entry and blocks (`blocks`, `fills`, `ground`); the full turtle API runs in that
  block world with real drops, recipes and tick timing (`docs/turtle.md`). Computers a turtle places boot when
  turned on (floppies, drives, monitor walls and modem blocks work); `craftos_run` returns them under `computers`.
- Saved worlds live in `worlds/` (`worldFile: "advanced-peripherals-demo"`). A world's `deploy` list assembles the
  computer from workspace folders like an installer would, and `kind: "pocket"` gives a 26x20 terminal.
- Chests that scripts index beyond 27 slots need `size: 54`; out-of-range slots raise errors like real CC.
- Pass `timeScale` (e.g. 20) to `craftos_run`, `craftos_test` or `craftos_session_create` to run the virtual clock
  faster: `sleep(20)` then takes about one real second, and `os.clock()`/`os.epoch()` report the virtual time.
  `timeoutMs` stays in real time. Code that never yields is aborted after 7 s like CC.
- The terminal is 51x19; output that scrolls off is not in the captured text. Log to a file or print less when
  verifying.

## Addons (other mods)

Every mod besides CC:Tweaked is an addon. Switch on only the ones the user's modpack has, so a program cannot come to
rely on a peripheral their server lacks: `world.addons` in a world file, `CRAFTOS_ADDONS` in the MCP server's
environment, `"addons"` in craftos.json, or `--addons` on the command line. Each takes addon ids (a list in JSON,
separated by commas elsewhere), `"all"` or `"none"`; with no setting at all, everything the Minecraft version has is
on. A peripheral of an addon that is off fails the world at boot and names the addon. `craftos_info` lists what is on
and `craftos_help` lists every id. An addon only runs on the Minecraft versions its mod came out for; a mod that also
came out for 1.18.2 behaves as its 1.18.2 version on 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 too, so `world.version: "1.18.2"` gives the
most complete simulation.

- Advanced Peripherals 0.7.31r (`advanced-peripherals`): player, energy and environment detectors, chat box, redstone
  integrator, NBT storage, AR controller, ME and RS bridges, from fixtures (`docs/advanced-peripherals.md`,
  `worlds/advanced-peripherals-demo.json`).
- Mekanism 10.2.5 (`mekanism`, `mekanism-generators`): QIO, the Quantum Entangloporter, machines and reactors
  (`docs/mekanism-qio.md`, `worlds/mekanism-qio-demo.json`).
- Create, Tom's Peripherals (GPU screens appear in screenshots), Bigger and Extreme Reactors each have a doc in
  `docs/` and a demo in `worlds/`. CC's own `energy_storage` and `fluid_storage` work on any block
  (`docs/generic-storage.md`).

vhcctweaks (github.com/Akkiruk/vhcctweaks, a server mod for Vault Hunters on Minecraft 1.18.2) is an addon that is
OFF by default and not part of "all": switch it on by naming `vhcctweaks` in world.addons / CRAFTOS_ADDONS /
craftos.json addons, or with `world.vhcctweaks: "2.2.36"` or `"2.2.37"` (`"2.2.35"` also accepted; `false` forces it
off). It needs `world.version: "1.18.2"`. It adds the `ccvault` API (player token balances, transfers with an approval
prompt, the computer's host), the `vhcc` sandboxed file store, lockdown, linked ender modems and the inventory
batch/watch methods; 2.2.37 adds player Gear Power/Temper/reputation/skills/stats reads, items inside container items
and `identify`. The 2.2.37 API is modelled from the mod's spec: identify's roll is the emulator's, not Vault Hunters'
(docs/vhcctweaks.md lists what is simulated and how faithfully).
Linked computers (ender modem links, remote peripherals) run in real time: on a slow or busy machine (many emulated
computers at once) a linked-peripheral call can time out, stall or behave inconsistently, so don't read a flaky
linked test as a bug in the program until it fails on a quiet machine too.

## Setting up the MCP server

The server is `npx -y craftos-mcp serve`, over stdio, and needs Node.js 22 or newer. Its first start downloads the
engine and builds the CC:Tweaked ROM, once (about a minute); the server answers straight away and the tools that run
computers wait for it. The computers' files are the folder the server starts in (`CRAFTOS_WORKSPACE` sets another).
`CRAFTOS_VERSION` (`1.21.1`, `1.20.1` or `1.18.2`) and `CRAFTOS_ADDONS` go in the server's `env`, or in a
`craftos.json` at the project root. On Windows, if a client cannot start `npx`, give it `cmd` with the arguments
`/c npx -y craftos-mcp serve`.

Codex, in `~/.codex/config.toml` (or `.codex/config.toml` in a trusted project), or
`codex mcp add craftos -- npx -y craftos-mcp serve`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.craftos]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "craftos-mcp", "serve"]
# a test run can take longer than the default 60 seconds per call
tool_timeout_sec = 300
```

VS Code with Copilot: the extension (below) registers the server by itself. Without it, `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "craftos": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "craftos-mcp", "serve"]
    }
  }
}
```

Copilot's own config files (`.mcp.json` at the workspace root, `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`) take the same entry
under `mcpServers` instead of `servers`.

Cursor, in `.cursor/mcp.json` (or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every project); the same `mcpServers` entry goes in
Windsurf's `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` and Claude Desktop's `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "craftos": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "craftos-mcp", "serve"] }
  }
}
```

Gemini CLI, in `.gemini/settings.json` (or `~/.gemini/settings.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "craftos": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "craftos-mcp", "serve"] }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add craftos -- npx -y craftos-mcp serve` (on native Windows,
`claude mcp add craftos -- cmd /c npx -y craftos-mcp serve`), or the plugin, which brings this guide as the
`cc-tweaked-dev` skill: `/plugin marketplace add Akkiruk/craftos-mcp`, then `/plugin install craftos-mcp@craftos-mcp`.

`CRAFTOS_TOOLS=core` offers a lean set of 17 tools instead of all 32, for clients that pay for every tool in every
request.

## The VS Code extension

The craftos-mcp extension (`Rogiedoji.craftos-mcp` on the Visual Studio Marketplace, also on Open VSX as
`Rogiedoji/craftos-mcp`) gives Copilot's agent mode the MCP server with no config, adds Run in CraftOS and Debug in
CraftOS (F5) for any `.lua` file, lists `*.test.lua` files in the Testing view, opens `*.world.json` files in a world
editor, and in Cursor and Windsurf offers to write their MCP config. Its command **Add Agent Instructions to
Workspace** writes these instructions for Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Claude Code into the open folder.

## Working on craftos-mcp itself

This section is for changes to the craftos-mcp repository (github.com/Akkiruk/craftos-mcp), not for Lua projects that
use it.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build                               # TypeScript: tsc -b
node scripts/build-rom.mjs --download       # rom/cc-1.121.0 from the real CC:Tweaked jar
node scripts/build-rom.mjs --download 1.18.2  # rom/cc-1.101.3, for Minecraft 1.18.2
npx vitest run                              # the tests; they need the engine and a ROM
npx prettier --check .                      # formatting, as CI checks it
```

`npm run setup` does all of it in one go and also downloads the prebuilt engine for your OS from the latest release
(or build it: `engine/build.cmd` on Windows, `engine/build.sh` elsewhere). CI only builds and checks formatting, so
run the tests locally before a pull request; CONTRIBUTING.md says what a change that executes Lua must come with.

- Engine fork: `engine/` (CMake). Client and protocol: `packages/rawterm`. Orchestration: `packages/runner`. MCP
  tools: `apps/mcp-server`. Command line: `apps/cli`. VS Code extension: `apps/vscode` (its own package and lockfile:
  `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit` inside it).
- The simulation (peripherals, modems, turtles, addons): `rom-overlay/rom/ccsim`. After changing it, copy it into
  each ROM (`cp -r rom-overlay/. rom/cc-1.121.0/`, and `rom/cc-1.101.3/` for 1.18.2) or rebuild the ROMs.
- AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/craftos-mcp.mdc` and the `cc-tweaked-dev`
  skills are generated from `scripts/agent-docs/`: edit those, then run `node scripts/build-agent-docs.mjs`
  (`--check` says whether any file is stale).
